tiles.title: Growing season
tiles.text: Usually from 24.04 to 14.10 (dd.mm). Heat sum GDD (>5 °C): 2855 °C·d/year. Mean temperature 9.7 °C, trend +0.35 °C per decade.
tiles.confidence_why: ~50 km grid; elevation correction -0.2 °C (POWER cell 310 m, field 338 m).

tiles.title: Frost
tiles.text: First autumn frost usually 14.10, in 1 in 10 years as early as 05.10. Coldest night in 1 in 10 winters: -31.4 °C. Sow warmth-loving crops (maize, soybean) after 03.05.
tiles.confidence_why: Frost pockets in valleys can get frost later than the grid shows.

tiles.title: Water balance
tiles.text: Months with a deficit (rain < ET₀): Jul, Aug, Sep. July: -63 mm, trend -11.8 mm per decade. Annual rainfall 840 mm, ET₀ 930 mm.
tiles.confidence_why: Rainfall from a reanalysis (~50 km cell) — local storms may differ.

tiles.title: Soil drought
tiles.text: Share of season months with clearly dry soil (z‑score < −1). Last 8 years: 15%, first 8 years: 15%.
tiles.confidence_why: GWETROOT root-zone moisture is a model (MERRA‑2), not a SMAP satellite measurement.

tiles.title: Heat
tiles.text: Earlier 38.0, recently 37.0 days/year (trend +2.3 per decade). Heat during flowering reduces grain set.
tiles.confidence_why: 2 m air temperature from the grid; ECOSTRESS (70 m) is planned as an extension.

tiles.title: Water erosion
tiles.text: Slope 1.6%, soil clay loam (K=0.0178). Downpours ≥ 20 mm: 8.4 days/year. Bare soil: 7.0 months/year.
tiles.confidence_why: LS from SRTM 30 m at the field point (assumed slope length 100 m); R from the Fournier index (Arnoldus), without rain intensity data.
tiles.source: SRTM 30 m (NASA/USGS, via OpenTopoData), SoilGrids 2.0 (ISRIC, 250 m)

tiles.title: Soil
tiles.text: Organic carbon 2.2% (≈ 3.8% humus). Sand 23%, silt 44%, clay 33%. Plant-available water ≈ 196 mm per 1 m of soil.
tiles.confidence_why: SoilGrids is a 250 m model — a single field may differ; a soil test is recommended.

sources.ndvi: MODIS MOD13Q1 NDVI 250 m (NASA, ORNL DAAC)
sources.egib: EGiB land register — soil class contours (GUGiK: ULDK + National Land Register Integration)

errors.ndvi: źródło niedostępne (ponowna próba za kilka minut)

GDD.text: Growing degree days — we add up how many degrees each day was warmer than the plant's growth threshold. It tells whether the crop gathers enough heat to ripen.

ET0.text: Reference evapotranspiration — how much water (mm) would evaporate from soil and well-watered grass. Computed with FAO‑56 from temperature, humidity, wind and radiation.

Kc.text: Crop coefficient — multiplier of ET₀ for a given crop and growth stage (e.g. maize in midsummer ≈ 1.2).

water_balance.text: Rainfall minus ET₀. A negative value means more water evaporates that month than falls as rain; plants then draw on soil reserves.

moisture_anomaly.text: How far soil moisture in a month departs from the long-term mean, in standard deviations (z‑score). Below −1 = clearly dry.

NDVI.text: Satellite greenness index (0–1). Below ~0.3 a field is usually bare or very sparsely vegetated.

RUSLE.text: Soil loss model for water erosion: A = R·K·LS·C·P (rain × soil erodibility × slope × plant cover × conservation practices).

humus.text: Soil organic matter. The balance uses reproduction/degradation coefficients (VDLUFA, Eich & Kundler): root crops deplete it, legumes and cover crops rebuild it.

soil_class.text: Soil quality class from the Polish land register (EGiB): I = best soils, VI = poorest. Letters before the class give the land use: R arable land, Ł meadows, Ps pastures. Classes IIIa/IIIb and IVa/IVb apply to arable land.

p90.text: The value not exceeded in 9 out of 10 years. “Last frost p90 = 15.05” means that only in 1 year in 10 does frost occur later.
